title: A 28nm 0.22μJ/Token Memory-Compute-Intensity-Aware CNN-Transformer Accelerator with Hybrid-Attention-Based Layer-Fusion and Cascaded Pruning for Semantic-Segmentation
problem: Hybrid CNN-Transformer models (ConvFormers) for semantic segmentation suffer from large token-length demands (>16K TL), creating three challenges: (1) sparse attention cannot buffer attention feature-maps on-chip at high sparsity, (2) layer-fusion is infeasible due to simultaneous K/V/weight buffering constraints, (3) low sparsity in segmentation head limits zero-skipping effectiveness.
motivation: Semantic segmentation is critical for autonomous driving and embodied intelligence, but ConvFormer's memory and compute intensity exceed accelerator on-chip capacity.
method: 28nm hybrid CNN-Transformer accelerator using memory-compute-intensity-aware dataflow, hybrid-attention-based layer-fusion avoiding redundant K/V and weight external-memory-access (EMA), and cascaded pruning targeting both backbone and segmentation head, achieving 0.22μJ/token.
key_novelty: Hybrid-attention layer-fusion addressing K/V EMA redundancy across fused layers, combined with cascaded pruning for low-sparsity segmentation head.
contributions: 0.22μJ/token energy efficiency for semantic segmentation on high-resolution (16K+ token) inputs
Hybrid-attention layer-fusion reducing redundant K/V and weight external-memory access
Cascaded pruning extending sparsity benefits to low-sparsity segmentation head
limitations: Absolute throughput (tokens/s), area, and latency not discussed; comparison with state-of-the-art transformer accelerators absent.
